facts.text: March Air Reserve Base began as Alessandro Flying Training Field in February 1918 and was renamed March Field on March 20, 1918, honoring Second Lieutenant Peyton C.
After the B‑52D retired in 1982, the 22d Bombardment Wing became the 22d Air Refueling Wing and first flew the KC‑10A Extender tanker.
In 1957, 22d Wing aircrews completed the longest nonstop mass flight ever, covering 5,840 miles from England to California.
March Airfield Museum CA, located on the historic airfield, showcases one of the oldest aviation sites in the United States.
The 1st Fighter Group’s aircraft were used in 1957 to film the Hollywood movie Jet Pilot, setting a 24‑plane formation record.
Since 1995, the former March AFB land has been managed by the March Joint Powers Authority, which hosts the California Air National Guard’s 144th Fighter Wing alert site.
